newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria contracts Total to run Kaduna refinery.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria contracts Total to run Kaduna refinery.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has contracted French oil company Total SA to run the activities of the Kaduna Refinery and Petrochemicals Company in the north for three years, state radio reported on Tuesday.
It said the contract valued at between $160 million to $220 million, included the cost of the turn around maintenance of the facility.
A spokesman for the company said in Paris on Monday that Total was in talks with Nigeria to offer technical assistance for the refinery but that no contract had been signed.
Total's Nigerian subsidiary, Total Nigeria Plc, was last month appointed a consultant on downstream operations in the oil industry, the failure of which has led to paralysing fuel shortages.

The failure of Nigeria's four poorly-maintained refineries to work close to their designed capacity of 445,000 barrels per day, as well as of the distribution network, has led to bouts of fuel scarcity which paralyse Africa's biggest crude oil producer for weeks at a time.
Local business and the World Bank have said that the best long term solution is to privatise the sector, but the military government appears reluctant to do so.
